project.boundarySource: Curated Oundle visitor boundary derived from ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024)
project.researchNotes: Full visitor audit completed 2026-08-08. Statutory records come from the locally bundled Historic England NHLE download. Every public planner item is inside the unchanged ONS Oundle boundary. Barnwell Country Park and other nearby countryside attractions remain outside the town planner. Historic England official list-entry date enrichment completed 2026-08-08: 162 of 170 statutory records now carry defensible date evidence; unresolved entries were individually checked and retained as unknown. Standalone attraction audit added 2026-08-08. These regional destinations are outside the active town boundary, appear only on Home discovery, and do not alter the town tourist rating.

touristAppeal.label: Local detour
touristAppeal.summary: Oundle qualifies as a local detour through Oundle historic town centre and Market Place and St Peter's Church. It is best treated as a shorter stop rather than a half-day destination.

townGuide.headline: Honey-stone streets, a soaring spire and an easy riverside pause
townGuide.intro: Begin in the Market Place, follow the church spire through warm limestone lanes and use the heritage trail to spot medieval fabric behind Georgian fronts. Add the museum, then pause at the Wharf or one of Oundle's cafés.
perfectFor: Visitors who enjoy architecture without crowds
A church, museum and riverside lunch

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Market Place, St Peter's and the Heritage Trail
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start in the Market Place, step inside St Peter's, then use the Heritage Trail through West Street and the school quarter. Add the museum on a weekend or finish with lunch at Oundle Wharf.

dontMiss: Oundle historic town centre and Market Place
townGuide.suggestedTime: Half a day; a full day with an exhibition or show
townGuide.visitorMood: Best for handsome streets, quiet history and independent cafés.

visitorHighlights.name: Oundle historic town centre and Market Place
visitorHighlights.reason: Explore a coherent limestone townscape of Georgian fronts, medieval fabric, independent shops and the landmark church spire.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Outdoor public streets and Market Place; best in daylight.

visitorHighlights.name: St Peter's Church
visitorHighlights.reason: Step into Oundle’s skyline landmark for a spacious medieval interior, carved details and the tall spire that orientates almost every town-centre view.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Usually daily 10:00-16:00; services can restrict access.

visitorHighlights.name: Oundle Museum
visitorHighlights.reason: Use the former courthouse to connect Oundle’s elegant streets with finds and stories stretching from prehistory and Roman settlement to the modern town.

visitorHighlights.name: The Talbot Hotel historic interiors and courtyard
visitorHighlights.reason: Pause in a Grade I coaching inn rebuilt in 1626, with stone linked to Fotheringhay Castle, a richly atmospheric courtyard and a staircase associated with Mary, Queen of Scots.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Public hospitality areas open with the hotel.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: The Talbot history and visitor information

visitorHighlights.name: Oundle School Cloisters and Great Hall streetscape
visitorHighlights.reason: Follow the public streets around the Cloisters, Great Hall, chapel and school buildings to see how centuries of collegiate architecture shape the centre of Oundle.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Exterior views from public streets; interiors restricted.

visitorHighlights.name: Oundle Wharf and River Nene
visitorHighlights.reason: Trade stone streets for a calm riverside pause at Oundle Wharf, where boats, the River Nene and waterside food give the town a gentler second character.

visitorHighlights.name: The Yarrow Gallery
visitorHighlights.reason: Catch a public exhibition in an attractive two-storey school gallery, where contemporary work and Oundle’s educational character meet in a more intimate cultural stop.

visitorHighlights.name: Stahl Theatre
visitorHighlights.reason: Book a public performance in a characterful 264-seat theatre converted from an 1865 church; it is a reason to extend an Oundle visit into the evening rather than a daytime drop-in sight.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Ticketed performances and advertised events only.
